title: Start deterministic Valve generator foundations without inventing Siemens contract facts
goal: Begin real GEN-VALVE-001 product development in parallel with OLQ-VALVE-PROFILE-001 by implementing only generator capabilities that are required by issue #62 and do not depend on the still-unqualified fbValve_Solenoid interface. Build deterministic output identity/manifest, safe output containment, centralized Siemens engineering-name and symbol validation/allocation, and stable input diagnostics now; defer exact Valve call parameters, dependency names, versions and instance/data ownership until #61 produces the verified V21 contract.
scope: Work only in Domain, PlcCompiler/IR, SiemensBackend, GeneratorCli, focused tests and examples listed in candidatePolicy.allowedPaths. Do not modify TiaV21Worker, workflows, agents, tasks, runner configuration, vendor payloads, or IndustrialMDE.

Add deterministic multi-artifact output manifest plumbing suitable for the upcoming Valve slice. The manifest must contain generator identity, deterministic input identity, an explicit externally supplied profile/contract identity token, and relative paths plus SHA-256 hashes for every generated PLC/source artifact. The manifest itself is not included in its own hash list; its bytes must nevertheless be deterministic. Do not fabricate a Valve profile identity or Siemens library metadata.

Derive input identity from a canonical representation of the normalized parsed input model, not from raw JSON whitespace, the input filename/path, output path, timestamps, locale, machine identity or other environment data. Semantically identical parsed input must have the same input identity.
Enforce output-root containment for every generated artifact and for the manifest before write. Reject absolute/escaping paths and traversal rather than normalizing them outside the requested root.

Introduce the smallest centralized Siemens engineering-name/symbol policy needed for first-device generation: reject null/empty required names, invalid names that cannot be emitted safely, and case-insensitive duplicate allocated symbols. Do not silently rename user input unless an existing documented deterministic naming rule already requires it.

Add stable diagnostic codes/categories and locations for malformed or omitted required type tokens, unsupported enum tokens, null/empty required data, invalid names, duplicate symbols and output containment violations where those checks are independent of the final Valve FB interface.

Keep existing Motor UDT generation behavior and CLI usage compatible unless a strictly additive manifest/output/profile API is required. Do not convert the repository into a generic graph compiler, plugin framework, catalog abstraction, general SCL AST or UI platform.

Do not add any fbValve_Solenoid call, parameter name, dependency identity, version, DB requirement, multi-instance requirement, target-memory requirement or other Siemens fact that has not been proven by #61. The follow-up GEN-VALVE-001 completion step will bind these foundations to the verified contract.

requirements: Candidate changes are limited exactly to candidatePolicy.allowedPaths and Siemens.Engineering remains absent from Domain/PlcCompiler core.

Same normalized parsed input plus the same explicit profile identity produces the same input identity and byte-identical generated artifacts and manifest across repeated Linux runs, even when non-semantic JSON whitespace differs.

The deterministic manifest contains generator identity, canonical parsed-model input identity, explicit profile identity and SHA-256 for every generated PLC/source artifact. It lists only relative artifact paths, does not hash/include itself in its artifact hash list, and contains no timestamps, absolute input/output paths, locale, machine/user identity or other environment-specific data.
The manifest itself is emitted deterministically beneath the requested output root and repeated generation produces byte-identical manifest bytes.

Every output path is proven contained beneath the requested output root before write. Absolute paths, traversal and containment escapes fail with a stable diagnostic and do not write outside the root.
Null/empty required names, invalid engineering names and case-insensitive duplicate symbols fail with stable diagnostic codes/categories and locations rather than producing ambiguous SCL.
Malformed or omitted required type tokens and unsupported enum tokens fail rather than silently defaulting semantics.

Focused Linux tests cover canonical input identity across whitespace-only JSON differences, deterministic manifest/artifact bytes and hashes, duplicate/invalid-name rejection, malformed/omitted type, unsupported enum and output containment.
Existing Motor UDT generation and current Linux regressions remain green.
No code, example or test asserts any unqualified fbValve_Solenoid parameter, dependency, version, ownership, DB or target prerequisite fact.
